clips.send: Milledgeville. Where Georgia undid secession. October 1865: a convention here repealed secession, abolished slavery and refused to pay the Confederate debt — Johnson’s conditions. December 1865: the legislature ratified the 13th Amendment. The state prison here held Leo Frank in 1915 before a mob took him away.

clips.send: Atlanta. Railroad hub, “capital of the New South”. The 1867–68 convention met here and moved the capital from Milledgeville to Atlanta. Home of the International Cotton Exposition (1881) and the Cotton States Exposition (1895). Black colleges grew here: Atlanta University, Morehouse, Spelman, Clark. W. E. B. Du Bois taught at Atlanta University (1897–1910). Site of the 1906 race massacre and the 1913 Leo Frank trial.

clips.send: Macon. A minister turned lawmaker. Henry McNeal Turner, an AME church minister and former Union Army chaplain, organized Black voters across Georgia and was elected to the legislature from Bibb County (Macon) in 1868. When Black members were expelled in September 1868, Turner gave a fiery speech defending their right to serve. He later became a bishop and argued that Black Americans might find freedom only by leaving the US.

clips.send: Camilla. The 1868 Camilla massacre. September 1868: Black and white Republicans marched to a political rally in Camilla. Armed white men fired on the marchers; about a dozen Black people were killed. Violence like this — and Klan threats — kept many Black voters away from the polls that November.

clips.send: Savannah. “Forty acres” — promised, then taken back. January 1865: after meeting Black ministers in Savannah, General Sherman issued Field Order No. 15, setting aside coastal land in plots of up to 40 acres for freed families. About 40,000 people settled on that land — but President Johnson returned most of it to the former owners later in 1865. Savannah stayed Georgia’s main cotton port in the New South years.

clips.send: Marietta. Antisemitism and mob violence. Mary Phagan, the 13-year-old murder victim, was from Marietta. In August 1915 a mob took Leo Frank from the Milledgeville prison and lynched him near Marietta. Months later the Ku Klux Klan was refounded on nearby Stone Mountain; Jewish Georgians felt the danger for years.

clips.send: Darien (McIntosh County). Black political power on the coast. Tunis Campbell, a Freedmen’s Bureau agent from New Jersey, organized freedpeople on the coast and was elected state senator in 1868. He was one of the Black legislators expelled in 1868 and reseated in 1870. Opponents later had him jailed and sentenced to hard labor — a sign of how hard Black leaders were pushed out.

clips.send: Thomson. Voice of the Populists. Tom Watson, a lawyer from Thomson, led Georgia’s Populist Party in the 1890s for struggling farmers. In Congress he pushed for Rural Free Delivery: mail carried to farm families’ doors for free. After his political defeats he turned against Black and Jewish Americans, and his newspapers stirred hatred during the Leo Frank case.

clips.send: 米利奇维尔。佐治亚州在这里废除了脱离联邦的决定。1865 年 10 月，这里召开的会议废除了脱离联邦的法令、废除了奴隶制，并拒绝偿还邦联债务——满足了约翰逊的条件。 1865 年 12 月，州议会批准了第十三修正案。 1915 年，利奥·弗兰克被关押在这里的州监狱，后被暴徒劫走。

clips.send: 萨凡纳。“四十英亩土地”——许诺后又被收回。1865 年 1 月，谢尔曼将军在萨凡纳会见黑人牧师后发布第 15 号战地命令，把沿海土地划成最多 40 英亩的地块分给获得自由的家庭。 约 4 万人在这些土地上定居——但同年晚些时候，约翰逊总统把大部分土地还给了原来的主人。 在“新南方”时期，萨凡纳仍是佐治亚州最重要的棉花港口。

clips.send: 达里恩（麦金托什县）。海岸地区的黑人政治力量。图尼斯·坎贝尔来自新泽西州，是自由民局工作人员，他在海岸地区组织自由民，1868 年当选州参议员。 他是 1868 年被驱逐、1870 年恢复议席的黑人议员之一。 反对者后来让他入狱并被判苦役——可见黑人领袖受到了多么沉重的排挤。

clips.send: 梅肯。从牧师到议员。亨利·麦克尼尔·特纳是非洲卫理圣公会牧师、前联邦军随军牧师，他在全州组织黑人选民，1868 年从比布县（梅肯）当选州议员。 1868 年 9 月黑人议员被驱逐时，特纳发表了慷慨激昂的演说，捍卫他们任职的权利。 他后来成为主教，并认为黑人也许只有离开美国才能获得真正的自由。

clips.send: 汤姆森。平民党的代言人。汤姆森的律师汤姆·沃森在 19 世纪 90 年代领导佐治亚州的平民党，为困苦的农民发声。 他在国会推动“农村免费送信”：把信件免费送到农户家门口。 屡遭败选后，他转而攻击黑人和犹太人；在利奥·弗兰克案中，他办的报纸煽动仇恨。

clips.send: 玛丽埃塔。反犹主义与暴民暴力。13 岁的遇害者玛丽·费根来自玛丽埃塔。 1915 年 8 月，暴徒把利奥·弗兰克从米利奇维尔监狱劫走，在玛丽埃塔附近将他私刑处死。 几个月后，三K党在附近的石山重新成立；佐治亚州的犹太人多年生活在危险之中。

clips.send: 亚特兰大。铁路枢纽，“新南方之都”。1867—1868 年的制宪会议在这里召开，并把州首府从米利奇维尔迁到亚特兰大。 1881 年国际棉花博览会和 1895 年棉花州博览会在这里举办。 黑人高校在这里发展：亚特兰大大学、莫尔豪斯学院、斯佩尔曼学院、克拉克学院。杜波依斯曾在亚特兰大大学任教（1897—1910）。 1906 年种族屠杀和 1913 年利奥·弗兰克审判都发生在这里。
